record.file_problem: The post text is present; it refers to example outputs and an image that are not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The post applies a difference-in-means refusal-direction removal method to GPT-OSS 20B and measures refusal on JailbreakBench, testing the original intervention on a new model.
record.gate_note: The post reports system-prompt refusal rates, but those results do not test the refusal-direction claim. The supervised-fine-tuning result is described qualitatively and does not provide a reported refusal metric for a claim version. The post tests removal, but not adding the direction.
record.test_reason: Applies Arditi et al.'s difference-in-means refusal-direction ablation to gpt-oss-20b and measures refusal on JailbreakBench. Its own results bear on whether ablation removes refusal (V1). Because gpt-oss-20b reasons before answering, they also bear on V8. Implementation fidelity is uncertain: the author says vectors are 'subtracted' and suggests a 'skill issue'.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes that gpt-oss appears robustly safety-trained against system prompting and refusal-vector removal. Fine-tuning 'sort of worked', possibly through train/test overlap. The author also allows that the vector-removal failure may be an implementation 'skill issue'.
record.recipe_differences: The post derives harmful-minus-neutral mean activation vectors from hidden-layer outputs and subtracts a vector at layer outputs. It tests vectors across layers; it does not clearly specify projection at every position or report an addition experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The layer 13 vector is specifically reported to cause incoherence; refusal remained for all tested layers.
record.problems: Only 10 JailbreakBench samples were used per layer vector. No uncertainty estimate or unablated refusal baseline for the same sample set is stated. The layer 13 capability effect is described qualitatively, without a separate capability evaluation.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible claim-version results were left out. System-prompt results are not tests of the refusal-direction versions, and the fine-tuning outcome is qualitative.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; quantitative capability preservation.
No comparison with non-reasoning models, and no analysis of the reasoning trace.
No weight-edit abliteration; the ablation is applied at inference on layer outputs.

missing.what: Unablated refusal baseline: 99/100 refusals with no system prompt (different sample set from the ablation runs).

record.verdict_notes: This is a low-evidence blog post: 10 samples per layer, no uncertainty, and ablation described as subtracting a vector from layer outputs, possibly not orthogonal projection at all positions. The author flags possible implementation error, so the challenge verdicts should be weighted lightly. The text does not discuss gpt-oss as a reasoning model; the V8 link is based on that model property. Supervised fine-tuning and system-prompt results are not refusal-direction tests.

versions.untested_parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless requests was not tested. Capability preservation was not broadly measured; the post only reports incoherence for the layer 13 vector.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration result is reported.
No attack is tested as suppressing the refusal direction, and no training against ablation is reported.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account is reported.
The post does not separate harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is tested.
The post does not vary when or how refusal training is done to test whether that determines the existence of a removable direction.

statements.correction: lw:HfXyF4swFLpeLuv3W is an informal LessWrong post with linked code, not a README. The author says the failure may be a 'skill issue' (possible implementation error) and does not state a suspicion. The layer-13 vector caused incoherence while refusal stayed on all samples.
statements.problem: The numbers are right (24 layer vectors, 10 JailbreakBench samples, layer 13 incoherent). But the conditions lump lw:HfXy in with 'README-only evidence' although it is a LessWrong post. 'The author suspects an implementation error' overstates the author's hedge, 'Perhaps this is just a skill issue'.

Accurate for this study: each of 24 layer vectors, 10 JailbreakBench samples, all refused, harmful-minus-neutral prompts, text says 'subtract (ablate)'. One small point: 'suspects an implementation error' is stronger than the author's 'Perhaps this is just a skill issue'.

statements.correction: lw:HfXyF4swFLpeLuv3W tries each of the 24 per-layer diff-in-means vectors in turn, each described as subtracted from each layer output, on 10 JailbreakBench samples per vector. All samples were refused for every vector. The layer-13 vector caused incoherence. Unablated, with no system prompt, 99/100 of 100 JailbreakBench samples were refused.

The text loops over the 24 per-layer vectors and describes subtracting the vector 'from each layer output'. The 99/100 baseline is from Strategy 0 (no system prompt, 100 samples), not the 10-sample ablation set.
